plan: Since this auction functions as a second-price mechanism (sealed bids act as exit points in an ascending clock, and the winner pays the second-highest bid), truthful bidding is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value of $15 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and never overpay. There's no incentive to bid above or below my true value in this format.

Since the sealed bid acts as an exit price in an ascending clock auction with the winner paying the second-highest bid, this mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction. The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, as this maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids—bidding higher risks overpaying, bidding lower risks losing profitable wins.

Since this functions as a second-price auction (the sealed bid acts as my maximum willingness to pay, and I only pay the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $42 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, and I pay less than my value, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities.
